articleTitle: Spinalonga: Why It Was Fortified and How the Island’s Uses Changed
targetAudience: Readers interested in East Crete history

editorialCore.centralQuestion: What does Spinalonga: Why It Was Fortified and How the Island’s Uses Changed show through controlled evidence?
editorialCore.thesis: The plan follows controlled evidence and preserves unresolved questions.
editorialCore.viewerValue: A careful orientation to supported historical context.

factualScope.claim: Work on the Venetian fortress began in June 1579.
Bressani proposed the first enclosure; Orsini’s 1584 intervention added an upper defensive line.
factualScope.uncertainty: Do not call either sole creator

factualScope.claim: Its position served the harbour and approaches to Elounda within a wider defensive response.
Salt production formed part of the local strategic economy.
An earlier wall is now interpreted as Byzantine, probably 7th–8th c.
factualScope.uncertainty: UNESCO tentative text says antiquity; do not collapse disagreement

factualScope.claim: The fortress surrendered on 4 October 1715 after a three-month siege.
UNESCO’s nomination reports 1,112 people in 1881 and roughly 200 houses/25 shops later in the century.
The 1903 selection was connected with removal of remaining Muslim residents.
Law 463 identified Spinalonga for settlement; first arrivals followed in 1904.
factualScope.uncertainty: Dates/title must be checked in Gazette facsimile

factualScope.claim: A scholarly chapter reports 251 people transferred on 13 October 1904.
factualScope.uncertainty: Needs primary transport or gazette confirmation

factualScope.claim: Early food, housing and medical provision were severely inadequate.
Sulphone treatment changed the medical context in the 1940s.
An inscription credits the Brotherhood and its president Remoundakis with the 1939 perimeter road.
factualScope.uncertainty: Does not prove every claimed reform

factualScope.claim: Much leprosarium-era fabric was demolished in the 1980s.
factualScope.uncertainty: Not evidence that records were burned/destroyed

factualScope.claim: On Greece’s Tentative List since 2014; not inscribed on the World Heritage List.
factualScope.uncertainty: Never call it a World Heritage Site
